newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FORECAST-No change to Swedish repo rate Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-No change to Swedish repo rate Tuesday.

text.p: Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, will not lower its key interest rate, the repo rate, at its weekly Tuesday operation, a Reuters poll of 10 economists showed on Monday.
The main reason cited was the crown's weakness.
"The key reason is that the crown is so weak but also the line from the Riksbank that monetary policy is well balanced is playing a part," said Knut Hallberg, Swedbank economist.
Economists expected the crown to stage a recovery and forecast more cuts in the repo rate further down the track.
"The weakening of the crown is very liquidity driven now and really has not got much to do with fundamentals," said Peter Lindquist, economist at HSBC Midland Bank.
"When all the fundamentals are in place we will get a stronger crown."
Economists said this, combined with the fact that the Riksbank does not have an exchange rate target but an inflation goal, gave more weight to the expectation of a further lowering in the repo rate.
The repo rate, which is the Riksbank's key tool for controlling money market liquidity, currently stands at 4.10 percent. It was last lowered on December 17.
Economists interviewed for the poll were from Carnegie, Chase, Consensus, Handelsbanken, HSBC Midland Bank, PaineWebber, Salomon Brothers, S-E-Banken, Swedbank, and Tranferator.
